[CARCA](https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.06519) supports target-to-history cross-attention for recommendation; the following is an implementation proposal, not a published SASRec recipe. Encode history once; expose an immutable, explicitly passed context containing causal states, projected keys/values, padding mask and prefix positions. Score candidate c at prefix t as SASRec’s dot product plus a learned candidate-conditioned attention residual. Attend only to nonpadding positions j≤t, excluding the next-item target. Cache context per batch/request; never store mutable “last history” on the model. Full-catalog inference reuses the final-prefix context across candidate chunks and maintains running top-k. This reduces peak memory, but still requires attention computation for every candidate.

For training, chunk the positive plus 64 negatives and, if necessary, prefix positions; avoid materializing B×L×65×L attention weights. Use an explicit broadcastable prefix-and-padding mask: PyTorch SDPA boolean True means allowed, and rectangular is_causal masks use upper-left alignment. Set attention dropout to zero during evaluation. [SDPA documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention). For additive BCE, sum chunk losses with one global normalization and accumulate gradients before one optimizer step. To release chunk graphs while preserving encoder gradients, use detached context leaves, accumulate their gradients, then backpropagate those gradients through the original context once. Simply summing chunk losses retains their graphs. Sampled softmax requires a denominator spanning all chunks. [Autograd documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/autograd.html).

Before trials, test future-token perturbations leave earlier scores unchanged; empty histories produce finite scores and zero attention residual; candidate chunk sizes/order preserve scores and top-k; chunked gradients match an unchunked reference; intervening history requests cannot alter saved-context scores; and training-prefix scores match inference using identical sequence positions, weights and disabled dropout.
